system: Schelling credible commitment — REAL WTO retaliation data fit (SESSION-25)
data_source: Horn-Mavroidis WTO Dispute Settlement Dataset (World Bank, 2011 update of 2006 cutoff) + WTO Official Case Summaries 2010 Edition + per-dispute manual outcome coding
hypothesis_interpretation: FRAMING-LIKELY: WTO real data MISSES its own anchor → pre-reg (s_low/s_high, p_low/p_high) coords are mis-stated for WTO

data_rows.title: Australia – Salmon
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:arb_req_no_auth + WTO_ds18sum: Australia issued AQIS July 1999 lifting import ban; June 2000 mutual agreement
data_rows.notes: Settled bilaterally before authorisation; classic "threat-induced compliance"

data_rows.title: EC – Hormones (US)
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:auth_granted + imp_req_date populated + WTO_ds26: US retaliation applied 1999; EC never complied (still unresolved 2010+, MoU 2009)
data_rows.notes: Authorisation $116.8M; US tariffs imposed; EC refused to lift hormone ban

data_rows.title: EC – Bananas III
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:auth_granted + imp_req_date populated + WTO_ds27: EC Tariff-Only regime 1 Jan 2006 + 2009 Geneva Agreement
data_rows.notes: Authorisation $191.4M; US/Ecuador tariffs imposed; EC eventually adopted tariff-only regime under retaliation pressure

data_rows.title: Brazil – Aircraft
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:auth_granted + imp_req_date populated + WTO_ds46: PROEX III brought into compliance Aug 2001 DSB adoption
data_rows.notes: CAN $344M authorisation; Brazil modified PROEX three times under retaliation threat; final PROEX III ruled compliant

data_rows.title: EC – Hormones (Canada)
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:auth_granted + imp_req_date populated + WTO_ds48: parallel to DS26; EC never complied with hormones ruling
data_rows.notes: Canada $11.3M authorisation; same fundamental EC non-compliance as DS26

data_rows.title: Canada – Dairy
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:arb_susp_date populated + WTO_ds103: Canada eliminated Special Class 5 milk pricing
data_rows.notes: Settled during arb suspension; Canada changed measures

data_rows.title: US – FSC
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:auth_granted $4.043B + imp_req_date 2003 + WTO_ds108: US replaced FSC with ETI; ETI also struck down; EC tariffs applied 2004-2006; only AJCA 2004 partially compliant
data_rows.notes: Largest authorisation in WTO history; US compliance contested for years

data_rows.title: Canada – Dairy
data_rows.outcome_basis: Duplicate of DS103 with NZ as complainant; same outcome
data_rows.notes: Linked to DS103

data_rows.title: US – 1916 Act (EC)
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:auth_granted but unspecified value + WTO_ds136: 1916 Antidumping Act repealed Dec 2004 by US Congress
data_rows.notes: US complied just after authorisation by repealing the Act; pending claims resolved

data_rows.title: US – Section 110(5) Copyright
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:auth_granted but arb suspended Feb 2002 + WTO_ds160: 2003 mutual agreement on compensation; US paid lump sum
data_rows.notes: Settled with compensation rather than compliance per se; EC accepted ~€3.3M lump sum

data_rows.title: US – 1916 Act (Japan)
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:arb_susp_date Feb 2002 + Act repealed Dec 2004 + WTO_ds162: parallel to DS136
data_rows.notes: Same Act repeal as DS136

data_rows.title: US – Byrd Amendment
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:auth_granted Formula + imp_req_date + imp_date populated + WTO_ds217: Byrd Amendment repealed Feb 2006 (Deficit Reduction Act)
data_rows.notes: Multiple complainants retaliated; US Congress repealed amendment under pressure

data_rows.title: Canada – Aircraft Credits
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:auth_granted but no retaliation applied + WTO_ds222: Canada Account program modified to compliance
data_rows.notes: Canada changed Canada Account guidelines

data_rows.title: US – Byrd Amendment
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:auth_granted + imp_req_date + imp_date populated + WTO_ds234: parallel to DS217; same Feb 2006 repeal
data_rows.notes: Linked to DS217

data_rows.title: Japan – Apples
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:arb_susp_date 38203 + WTO_ds245: Japan implemented new measures, mutual agreement Aug 2005
data_rows.notes: Japan changed apple import quarantine rules

data_rows.title: US – Softwood Lumber IV
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:arb_susp_date + WTO_ds257: Settled by Oct 2006 Softwood Lumber Agreement
data_rows.notes: Multi-dispute negotiated settlement; all SLB disputes resolved bilaterally

data_rows.title: US – Softwood Lumber V
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:arb_susp_date + WTO_ds264: Settled by Oct 2006 SLA
data_rows.notes: Same SLA package

data_rows.title: US – Upland Cotton
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:auth_granted 40056 + WTO_ds267: US never fully removed GSM-102 export credit guarantees; Brazil/US 2014 MoU only after years more pressure
data_rows.notes: 2005 auth but compliance partial/late; coded as 24-mo non-compliance

data_rows.title: US – Oil Country Tubular Goods
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:arb_susp_date + WTO_ds268: US zeroing methodology disputes settled across many cases
data_rows.notes: Argentina pursued; settled via methodology changes

data_rows.title: US – Softwood Lumber VI
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:arb_susp_date + WTO_ds277: Part of Oct 2006 SLA package
data_rows.notes: Same SLA

data_rows.title: US – Gambling Services
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:auth_granted $21M + WTO_ds285: US never modified gambling restrictions; Antigua never retaliated effectively (small economy)
data_rows.notes: Authorised but compliance not achieved; tiny complainant ineffective

data_rows.title: EC – Biotech
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:arb_susp_date Feb 2008 + WTO_ds291: EC adopted new biotech approval process, complainants stood down
data_rows.notes: Settled to procedural improvements

data_rows.title: US – Zeroing (EC)
data_rows.outcome_basis: HM:arb_susp_date Sep 2010 + WTO_ds294: US modified zeroing methodology across many cases through 2012
data_rows.notes: Methodology changed gradually
